title: Altered Mental Status (AEIOU-TIPS)
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Altered Mental Status
Standard EM references (AEIOU-TIPS mnemonic); ACEP clinical policy on altered mental status

changelog.change: Initial entry — first moves, the AEIOU-TIPS differential with workup, and the can't-miss conditions table + pearls.

summary: First move is always a fingerstick glucose. In anyone malnourished, alcohol-dependent, or where there is any doubt, give thiamine 100 mg IV BEFORE glucose. Never assume 'psychiatric' or 'baseline' — organic causes are missed daily in patients labelled frequent fliers.

body.text: Fingerstick glucose first. If malnourished / alcohol-dependent / uncertain: thiamine 100 mg IV before dextrose — a glucose load in a thiamine-depleted patient can precipitate Wernicke's.

rows: Level, thiamine, LFTs; tremor + tachycardia = withdrawal; seizure risk peaks 24–48 h
Postictal; non-convulsive SE; glucose extremes; thyroid storm; myxoedema; Addisonian crisis
Glucose; TSH/T4; cortisol; EEG if postictal not clearing by 30 min
Hypoglycaemia; benzos, opioids, TCAs, salicylates; toxidromes
ABG + CO-oximetry; SpO2 unreliable with CO; high-flow O2 now
TBI; ICH; subdural (delayed in the elderly after a minor fall); hypo/hyperthermia
Meningitis; encephalitis; septic encephalopathy; abscess; UTI in the elderly
LP if no focal deficit / papilloedema; empiric antibiotics BEFORE CT if bacterial meningitis is likely
Diagnosis of exclusion — rule out organic causes first
Ischaemic stroke (esp. posterior); ICH; SAH (thunderclap); CNS mass
Head CT; CTA if LVO concern; LP if CT negative + thunderclap headache
Full triad (confusion + ophthalmoplegia + ataxia) present in only ~16% — needs high suspicion
Thiamine 500 mg IV q8h ×3 days, before glucose; risk: alcohol, malnutrition, hyperemesis, GI surgery, TPN
Asterixis; fetor hepaticus; identifiable precipitant (bleed, infection, constipation, meds)
Lactulose 30 mL q1–2h until a bowel movement; rifaximin for maintenance; treat the precipitant
SBP usually > 220; headache + confusion + visual change; PRES on MRI
Labetalol or nicardipine IV; lower MAP by 20–25% over the first hour — avoid rapid normalisation
Persistent AMS after an apparent seizure; subtle eye deviation, facial twitching, automatisms
EEG is diagnostic; treat per the SE ladder; LP for encephalitis if febrile

body.text: Minimum workup for undifferentiated AMS: glucose + BMP + CBC + UA + tox screen + non-contrast head CT. Elderly: subdural from a forgotten fall, UTI-triggered delirium, polypharmacy (anticholinergics, benzos, opioids, digoxin). SAH: CT sensitivity falls from ~98% within 6 h to ~85% at 24 h — LP any thunderclap headache with a negative CT. Meningitis: do not delay antibiotics for a CT unless there is a focal deficit, papilloedema, seizure, or immunocompromise.
